summary: An on/off switch for a single setting, with its label, description and error beside it, taking part in forms.

label.note: Visible label next to the switch and its accessible name. Names the setting, not the state: it does not change when the switch is toggled. Required: shadow DOM keeps an external <label for> from naming the inner control.

hideLabel.note: Visually hides the label; it stays the accessible name. Use only when the row has other visible text naming the setting.

description.note: Help text under the label: what turning the setting on does.

error.note: Error message. Setting it marks the field invalid and blocks form submission (customError).

size.note: Track and thumb size: default 32x20 track with a 16px thumb, sm 24x16 track with a 12px thumb. The label and description keep their size.

value.note: Submitted with the form while on. Nothing is submitted while off.

checked.note: On (true) or off (false). Not reflected: the attribute is the default restored by form reset.

required.note: Must be on for the form to submit (native valueMissing). Adds an aria-hidden asterisk after the label.

disabled.note: Cannot be focused or toggled; dimmed; not submitted. A disabled fieldset ancestor has the same effect without changing this prop.

anatomy.name: field
anatomy.notes: Grid: the switch in the first column; label, description and error in the second.

anatomy.name: control
anatomy.notes: Wrapper that stacks the input, the track and the thumb in one cell.

anatomy.name: input
anatomy.notes: The native on/off control, exposed as a switch; receives focus, Space and validation. Covers the track so a click anywhere on it toggles.

anatomy.name: track
anatomy.notes: Pill-shaped track; its fill shows on or off.

anatomy.name: thumb
anatomy.notes: Round thumb inset inside the track; at the inline start when off and the inline end when on.

anatomy.name: required-indicator
anatomy.notes: Asterisk, hidden from assistive technology (required is exposed natively).

anatomy.name: error
anatomy.notes: Persistent polite live region; text appears when invalid.

input.note: Each toggle by the user. Native and composed, so it crosses the shadow boundary.

change.note: Toggle committed by the user; read checked from the target. Re-dispatched from the host because native change is not composed. Not fired when checked is set in code or by form reset.

hover.note: Pointer cursor only; no color change (none in the visual reference).

focus-visible.note: 3px solid ring around the track (a translucent ring would fall under 3:1).

checked.note: Track fills with the primary color and the thumb moves to the inline end: state is shown by position as well as color.

invalid.trigger: error set, or required and off after blur or a submit attempt

disabled.trigger: disabled prop, or a disabled fieldset ancestor

accessibility.accessibleNameSource: The label prop, through a native <label for> in the same shadow root.

formAssociation.note: ElementInternals: form value is value only while on (null while off); validity mirrored from the inner input (required -> valueMissing, error -> customError); formResetCallback restores the default checked state (the checked attribute); formStateRestoreCallback restores checked; a disabled fieldset disables it without touching the disabled attribute, and a disabled switch is not submitted.

accessibility.targetSize: Track is 32x20 (default) or 24x16 (sm); the label next to it is part of the clickable row and the 12px gap satisfies the WCAG 2.5.8 spacing exception. With hide-label, keep stacked switches at least 24px apart.
accessibility.focusRingVisible: On keyboard focus of the input; 3px solid ring in switch.focus-ring.color around the track.
accessibility.missingNameWarning: Dev-only console warning, once, when label is empty.

keyboard.Tab: move focus to and from the switch
keyboard.Enter: submits the form (implicit submission; the control has no form owner in its shadow root, SB-0009); does not toggle

aria: role="switch" on the native checkbox input; on/off is exposed from its checked state (aria-checked true/false), never mixed
aria-describedby -> description and error ids (same root)
required: native required; the asterisk is aria-hidden
error: sets a customError validity, so the form blocks submission
the label names the setting and does not change with the state
announcements: state change is announced natively as on/off when toggled
error text is announced once when it appears (persistent aria-live=polite region)

useCases.when: A single setting that is either on or off (notifications, dark mode, airplane mode)
useCases.use: sb-switch with a label naming the setting

useCases.when: The effect of turning it on needs explaining

useCases.use: one sb-switch per setting, each with its own name; only those that are on are submitted

useCases.when: The setting must be on before the form can be sent
useCases.use: required, with a label that states what is being turned on

antiPatterns.pattern: A label that changes with the state ("On"/"Off", "Enabled"/"Disabled")
antiPatterns.why: The switch's state is already exposed as on/off; a changing label makes the name and the state contradict each other (WAI-ARIA APG switch pattern)
antiPatterns.alternative: A fixed label naming the setting

antiPatterns.pattern: A switch for a partly-on (mixed) state
antiPatterns.why: A switch has only on and off; it cannot show or announce mixed

antiPatterns.pattern: Choosing one of several options, or several from a list
antiPatterns.why: A switch controls exactly one on/off setting
antiPatterns.alternative: Radio Group, or one Checkbox per option

drift.contract: label, description and error are props of Switch
drift.realization: the visual reference composes Field and Label around Switch; shadow DOM requires them inside

drift.contract: default track 32x20 (size.switch.*), thumb 16px with a 2px inset
drift.realization: the visual reference uses an 18.4px track; the semantic size tokens round it to the 4px grid
the visual reference uses its light input color, below 3:1; changed for WCAG 1.4.11
the visual reference uses the foreground color in dark mode; one semantic alias per component token, and color.background on color.input meets 3:1
the visual reference uses a translucent ring, below 3:1 (WCAG 1.4.11)

drift.contract: destructive border on the track and a built-in error message
drift.realization: the visual reference has no switch-specific invalid style
not reflected: the attribute is the default restored by form reset

openQuestions.question: Contract content drafted with the contract-author skill (visual reference, WAI-ARIA APG)?
openQuestions.answer: Yes: APG switch pattern for keyboard and ARIA; visual reference Switch for look, sizes and API; the project's Checkbox contract for the field layout and form behavior.

openQuestions.question: Which native control carries the switch: a checkbox input with role=switch, or a button with role=switch and aria-checked?
openQuestions.answer: Checkbox input with role=switch (recommended). It gives native Space toggling, required/valueMissing validation, disabled and the validity message for free, like Checkbox (SB-0007 native first). A button would need aria-checked, keyboard and validity rebuilt by hand. SB-0101.

openQuestions.question: Does Enter toggle the switch (APG lists it as optional) or submit the form?
openQuestions.recommendation: Enter submits the form; only Space toggles.
openQuestions.answer: Enter submits the form, like every other form control here (SB-0009), and does not toggle; Space toggles. This matches the native checkbox and keeps Enter meaning one thing across a form. SB-0101.

openQuestions.question: Is checked reflected to an attribute?
openQuestions.answer: No. The attribute is the default that form reset restores (like native defaultChecked), as in Checkbox.

openQuestions.question: What does the form receive while the switch is off?
openQuestions.answer: Nothing: value (default "on") is submitted only while on. An "off value" prop was discarded: it breaks the native contract every server already parses. SB-0101.

openQuestions.question: Which two sizes, and what do they change?
openQuestions.recommendation: default and sm, as in the visual reference; they change only the track and thumb.
openQuestions.answer: default (32x20 track, 16px thumb) and sm (24x16 track, 12px thumb), from the existing size.switch.* semantic tokens. Label and description keep their size so a form keeps one text size. SB-0101.

openQuestions.question: Is label required?
openQuestions.recommendation: Yes, with hide-label to hide it visually.
openQuestions.answer: Yes, like Checkbox and Input. hide-label keeps it as the accessible name.

openQuestions.question: Where is the label, and where does the thumb go when on in right-to-left text?
openQuestions.recommendation: Label after the switch; thumb at the inline end when on, mirrored in RTL.
openQuestions.answer: Label after the switch in the same row as Checkbox; on moves the thumb to the inline end, so it mirrors in RTL. A label-before layout is left to composition (later Field work). SB-0101.

openQuestions.question: Does the switch support indeterminate or readonly?
openQuestions.answer: No. A switch has only on and off (ARIA switch has no mixed state), and the native checkbox has no readonly; use Checkbox for mixed and disabled for unavailable. SB-0101.

openQuestions.question: Does the thumb animate?
openQuestions.recommendation: Yes, a short slide that is removed under reduced motion.
openQuestions.answer: Yes: the thumb slides and the track fill fades over motion.duration.fast; with prefers-reduced-motion the change is instant. SB-0101.

openQuestions.question: Manual screen-reader pass (VoiceOver, NVDA) of role=switch on a checkbox input.
openQuestions.recommendation: Run it during the a11y audit before stable.
openQuestions.answer: Scheduled for the a11y audit before stable (R1 requires that audit); automated axe and accessibility-tree checks cover beta.
